issue.title: Custom HTTP headers not passed in all Provider calls
issue.body:
# Environment tested against
- Pact JVM version: `au.com.dius.pact.provider:spring7:4.7.5`
- Pact Broker: `3.0.0-pactbroker2.121.2`

# Description
- The Pact JVM library provides the ability to add custom HTTP headers to all requests to the Pact Broker via the attribute `customHeaders` like so:
  ```java
  @PactBroker(
      url = "http://localhost:9292",
      authentication = @PactBrokerAuth(
          username = "pact",
          password = "pact"
      ),
      customHeaders = {
          @PactBrokerHttpHeader(name = "X-Pact-Broker-Client-Id", value = "local-id"),
          @PactBrokerHttpHeader(name = "X-Pact-Broker-Client-Secret", value = "local-secret")
      }
  )
  ```  
- These headers are not passed on all calls to the broker
- [this appears partially related to this issue](https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-jvm/issues/1917)

# Steps to reproduce
- I have created a project using Docker Compose, nginx, Pact JVM provider lib with Spring Boot test. This project runs the entire stack locally and shows the issue when the pact provider test is run. https://github.com/nick-m-b/pact-jvm-custom-header-issue

1. Configure a Provider test with `@PactBroker` including `customHeaders`, as shown above
2. Run the provider verification against a broker with at least one published pact
3. Inspect the HTTP requests received by the Pact Broker (e.g. broker access logs, or a proxy in front of it)

# Observed behaviour
- The initial call(s) used to discover/navigate to the pact(s) (e.g. fetching consumers, following HAL links) include the configured custom headers
- The follow-up call that fetches the actual pact JSON content from its source URL does **not** include the custom headers

# Expected behaviour
- Custom headers configured via `customHeaders` should be sent on every request made to the Pact Broker during a verification run, including the request that retrieves the pact content itself

# Real-world impact
- Any Pact Broker deployment/gateway that requires these headers on all endpoints (e.g. a proxy enforcing a client id/secret, or a WAF rule) will reject the pact-content request, causing provider verification to fail even though broker discovery succeeds

issue.title: V4Pact.mergeInteractions drops metadata.plugins from later @Pact methods
issue.body:
`V4Pact.mergeInteractions` keeps only the first pact's metadata, dropping plugin config from other `@Pact` methods

## Summary

When a JUnit5 (or JUnit4/Spock) consumer test declares multiple `@Pact` methods for the same consumer/provider pair, the extensions merge the resulting pacts by calling `mergeInteractions(interactions: List<Interaction>)` on the first pact with each subsequent pact's interactions. `V4Pact`'s implementation only merges the interaction lists and always keeps `this.metadata`:

```kotlin
// V4Pact.kt
override fun mergeInteractions(interactions: List<Interaction>): Pact {
  return V4Pact(consumer, provider, merge(interactions).toMutableList(), metadata, source)
}
```

Any content stored under `metadata.plugins[].configuration` by a plugin's `ConfigureInteraction` response for a *later* `@Pact` method never reaches the merged pact.

## Impact

The pact-avro-plugin (https://github.com/zirekhq/pact-avro-plugin) stores each interaction's Avro schema pact-wide, keyed by a schema hash, in `metadata.plugins[].configuration`. When a consumer test has one `@Pact` method per `.avsc` file, only the first method's schema survives the merge. Provider verification then fails with:

```
Plugin Avro Schema configuration item with key '<hash>' is required
```

Reproduction: https://github.com/nathandeamer/pact-sample-avro

Confirmed on Slack (thanks @rholshausen) that this also affects the Protobuf plugin, just less visibly, since consumer tests there tend to reuse one proto file across `@Pact` methods, and that the metadata drop is not intentional.

## Root cause

`mergeInteractions(interactions: List<Interaction>): Pact` on the `Pact` interface only receives the other pact's interactions, never its metadata, so no implementation can merge `metadata.plugins` even if it wanted to. This is called directly by:

- `PactConsumerTestExt.kt` (JUnit5) — two call sites
- `BaseProviderRule.java` (JUnit4)
- `PactConsumerSpockExt.kt` (Spock)

## Proposed fix

Add an additive overload to the `Pact` interface:

```kotlin
fun mergeInteractions(other: Pact): Pact = mergeInteractions(other.interactions)
```

`V4Pact` overrides it to also merge `this.metadata` and `other.metadata`'s `plugins` lists by plugin `name`, deep-merging `configuration` for a name present in both (mirroring `PactBuilder.addPluginConfiguration`'s own use of `deepMerge`). `RequestResponsePact`/`MessagePact` (V3, no plugin metadata) keep the default. Then switch the four call sites above to the new overload.

Happy to open a PR with this change if it sounds right.

`minArrayLike` does not respect minLength when specifiying examples
issue.body: The `minArrayLike` matcher does make sure that the amount of items is asserted against, but does not provide the necessary amount of examples when generating the consumer test data. In my opinion, the `minArrayLike` call without `numExamples` should be identical to a call with  `numExamples`, with the `numExamples` value being the `minSize`. This problem occured with async messaging, not sure if this applies to sync messaging as well.

issue.title: 4.6.17 is breaking our headers setup
issue.body:
Hi,

We have one pact test that breaks when we try to migrate to pact version 4.6.17:

```kotlin
  @Pact(consumer = SERVICE_CONSUMER_PROVIDER)
  fun test(builder: PactBuilder): V4Pact {
    return builder
        .expectsToReceiveHttpInteraction("test") { httpBuilder ->
          httpBuilder
              .withRequest { httpRequestBuilder ->
                httpRequestBuilder
                    .path("/test")
                    .method("GET")
                    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                    .header("Accept", regexp("application/json.*", "application/json, application/*+json"))
              }
              .willRespondWith { httpResponseBuilder ->
                httpResponseBuilder
                    .status(200)
              }
        }
        .toPact()
  }
```

we always get the error:

```
Expected 'application/*+json' to match 'application/json.*'
```

So with the new version it seems to separate the header `application/json, application/*+json` into multiple strings.

I would expect that with the update this pact still works as before.

issue.title: OptionalBody.toV4Format() crashes on non-JSON bodies with a "+json" content-type suffix
issue.body:
## Summary

`OptionalBody.toV4Format()` assumes any content type ending in a `+json` structured syntax
suffix (RFC 6839 — e.g. `application/vnd.foo+json`) is parseable JSON, and only skips that
assumption when the body's `contentTypeHint` is `BINARY`. If the hint is `TEXT` (or unset)
and the body isn't actually JSON, `JsonParser.parseString(...)` throws, and that exception is
**uncaught** — it propagates all the way up and fails the entire pact-file write, not just
the one interaction.

## Repro

Found while adding Lua plugin support to `pact-plugins` (a JWT content-matcher plugin whose
body is a compact JWT: `header.payload.signature` — not JSON — under content type
`application/jwt+json`). Full write-up with exact file/line references and a working
workaround: https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-plugins/blob/lua-plugins/docs/known-issues/consumer-dsl-plugin-config-inconsistencies.md#issue-2-json-suffixed-content-types-are-assumed-to-be-parseable-json-when-writing-pact-files-and-only-a-binary-content-type-hint-bypasses-this---text-doesnt-and-pact-jvm-doesnt-degrade-gracefully-like-pact-reference-does

Relevant code:
- `ContentType.isJson()` (`core/model/src/main/kotlin/au/com/dius/pact/core/model/ContentType.kt:19`)
  — true for any `+json` suffix, regardless of hint.
- `OptionalBody.toV4Format()` (`core/model/src/main/kotlin/au/com/dius/pact/core/model/OptionalBody.kt:169`)
  — only bypasses the JSON-parse attempt when `contentTypeHint == BINARY`; otherwise calls
  `JsonParser.parseString(valueAsString())` uncaught.

## Comparison with pact-reference

`pact-reference`'s Rust equivalent (`OptionalBody::to_v4_json`, `pact_models::bodies`) has the
exact same "is `+json`? attempt parse" logic, but **catches** the parse failure and falls back
to base64-encoding the body with a warning log instead of crashing.

## Suggested fix

1. Catch the `JsonException` in `toV4Format()` and fall back to base64 (matching
   `pact-reference`'s existing graceful degradation), instead of letting it propagate.
2. Consider also skipping the JSON-parse attempt when `contentTypeHint == TEXT` (not just
   `BINARY`) — currently an explicit `TEXT` hint doesn't help at all for `+json`-suffixed
   types, which is surprising given a plugin author affirmatively said "treat this as plain
   text."

## Current workaround

Hint the body `BINARY` instead of `TEXT` — see `plugins/jwt/plugin.lua` in the linked repo.
